lessons.topic: Ask AI to show its working
lessons.bigIdea: You get a better answer when you ask it to think in steps and to name what it is unsure about.
lessons.useCase: Next time you compare two phones or plan a day out, ask for three options, the tradeoffs, and what it is least sure about.
lessons.proTip: If the answer feels vague, reply with one more detail, such as Perth and a budget.

lessons.bigIdea: A good prompt is a recipe you can use again, not a one-off lucky guess.
lessons.useCase: When a reply finally sounds like you, copy the prompt into a note called Prompt recipes.
lessons.proTip: Give each recipe a plain name, like Rewrite this text, short and kind.

lessons.bigIdea: AI is a fast first draft. You still choose what gets sent, booked, or bought.
lessons.useCase: Ask for a draft email, then change one sentence so it sounds like you before you send it.
lessons.proTip: Never paste passwords, bank codes, or private medical details into a chat.
